text:
Marcus Lin: Quick review request on the default role matrix (RBAC v2) before we cut policy bundle v0.1 -> v0.2. Specifically: who gets `audit_log.export` (CSV/JSON + SIEM push). Right now draft gives Org Admin + Security Admin. @Dr. Aisha Rahman @Olga Petrov @Kevin Osei @Naomi Feldman can you sanity check separation-of-duties here? We got a couple enterprise questionnaires asking for “audit export separate from billing + org admin”.

Naomi Feldman: +1, we’ve got PM-912 language that says “Security Admin manages audit logs” but I think we added Org Admin for convenience so customers don’t get blocked day 1.

Kevin Osei: From audit-logging side: export includes actor ids + IPs + sometimes redacted request metadata. Even if no payloads, it’s still sensitive (it’s basically an org’s activity trail). I’d rather keep export behind a narrower role.

Olga Petrov: For SOC2/ISO narratives, we want separation of duties: the folks who can change org settings / create keys shouldn’t automatically be the folks who can exfil audit history. Also some customers treat audit logs as “security monitoring data” and want it walled off.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Agree. Please do NOT default audit-log export to Org Admin. Too broad. Org Admin is already extremely powerful; adding log export makes it harder to claim least privilege.
Dr. Aisha Rahman: Default should be: Security Admin can export; Org Admin can view audit logs in-console (read) but not export/stream. If customer wants Org Admin to export, they can create a custom role or explicitly grant.

Marcus Lin: Got it. To be clear: you’re ok with Org Admin having `audit_log.read` but not `audit_log.export`.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. And console UX should reflect it (disable export button + show “Requires Security Admin”).

Felix Schneider: Works for UI. We already have a pattern for gated actions w/ a tooltip + “request access” copy. We’ll need the exact reason code for the 403 so we can show something non-scary.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Implementation detail: we currently treat `audit_log.export` as “read + bulk”. If we remove it from Org Admin, we should ensure `audit_log.read` still allows filtering / pagination (normal browsing) but blocks:
- “Download CSV/JSON”
- “Create export token / SIEM config”
- “Create export job (async)”

Kevin Osei: + streaming destination config (S3 bucket / Splunk HEC / etc) should definitely be Security Admin only.

Naomi Feldman: Question: what about Billing Admin? They sometimes need audit trails for invoices/usage disputes.

Olga Petrov: Billing Admin should not get audit export by default. If they need evidence for disputes, that’s “usage export” not “audit log export”. Different dataset, different controls.

Marcus Lin: Makes sense. We can also add a note in role definitions: billing disputes -> usage reports, not audit logs.

Connor O'Brien: From migration/rollout POV: changing defaults will cause some shadow-denies during dual-eval for orgs where people were relying on Org Admin for exports. We should:
1) make sure shadow-deny metric includes `audit_log.export`
2) add release note / doc blurb
3) add a one-time console banner in staging? maybe overkill.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: We can do the “soft landing”: during enforcement we return 403 with reason `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE_AUDIT_EXPORT` and we log a structured field. Console can catch and show CTA.

Felix Schneider: :thumbsup: If we have the reason code stable, I’ll wire it up.

Marcus Lin: Ok, proposal:
- Default role mapping:
  - Org Admin: `audit_log.read`
  - Security Admin: `audit_log.read`, `audit_log.export`, `audit_log.export_config.write`
  - Read-only: `audit_log.read` (??) or maybe none?

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Read-only should be able to view audit logs only if we can justify it. I’d prefer “Read-only” = product read-only (models, deployments, usage), not security telemetry. If customer wants an auditor role, that’s separate.

Olga Petrov: Agree. “Read-only” is too ambiguous for audits. We can add a default “Security Viewer” later if needed, but for now keep it minimal.

Kevin Osei: +1. We’ve already had a couple internal questions like “why does every engineer have access to audit logs?” Let’s not bake that in.

Naomi Feldman: Ok so Read-only gets no audit logs by default. That will be a change from current console behavior though (today org viewers can see some activity pages).

Kaitlyn Nguyen: We can keep the existing “Activity” view separate from “Audit Logs” (the audit log product is the compliance-grade trail). RBAC wise, we should treat “audit log” as its own resource; “activity feed” can remain less sensitive and may be covered by general read perms.

Marcus Lin: That’s a good distinction. We should document it so CS doesn’t get confused.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please do. Customers will ask. “Activity feed” != “audit log export.”

Marcus Lin: Action items:
- I’ll update role definitions doc: remove `audit_log.export` from Org Admin, move to Security Admin only. Add note on “Activity feed vs Audit log”.
- @Kevin Osei can you confirm the permission names we want for export + destination config? (I don’t want us to split/rename twice.)
- @Felix Schneider coordinate with @Kaitlyn Nguyen on 403 reason codes / UI copy.
- @Connor O'Brien we’ll add a migration note + watch shadow-denies for `audit_log.export` during Hosted canary.

Kevin Osei: For permissions, I’d suggest:
- `audit_log.read`
- `audit_log.export`
- `audit_log.export_destination.write` (create/update/delete SIEM/S3 destinations)
- `audit_log.export_destination.read`
Export job status can be covered by read.

Felix Schneider: Works. Please keep it consistent with existing console routes so I don’t end up with “export” vs “download” mismatches.

Naomi Feldman: I’ll update PM-912 requirements section to explicitly state: “Export defaults to Security Admin only.” We can position it as an enterprise-grade separation-of-duties improvement.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Thanks. One more: ensure Support role (impersonation) cannot export audit logs unless break-glass approved. This has bitten other vendors.

Marcus Lin: Good call. We’ll keep support impersonation path behind time-bounded elevated session and log it. Not granting `audit_log.export` to Support by default.

Kevin Osei: I’ll add an explicit audit event for “audit export initiated” including actor role ids + policy version, so it’s visible to customers.

Olga Petrov: Please also capture this decision in the RBAC v2 overview + control mapping notes. Auditors love these crisp boundaries.

Marcus Lin: Will do. I’ll post the updated matrix in this thread once I push.

Felix Schneider: :eyes: when ready. Also if we can add a short tooltip copy like “Audit log export requires Security Admin due to sensitive access” that’ll help.

Connor O'Brien: Tracking for rollout: I’ll add a dashboard filter for `audit_log.export` shadow-denies so we can see which orgs are going to complain.

Marcus Lin: Update: role matrix edited (draft) — Org Admin no longer has audit export. Will follow up with policy bundle PR shortly.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Approved direction. Keep it strict by default.
